correctness.rationale: Stochastic Fubini and Ito isometry give the exact target covariance and observation variance, so conditioning reduces the design to maximizing a positive scalar gain. In logarithmic coordinates the covariance integral is a marginal of a jointly log-concave density; Prékopa implies a nonincreasing logarithmic derivative, strictly decreasing by real analyticity and unequal endpoint slopes. The Gaussian variance fraction is nondecreasing in time. Their difference therefore crosses zero at most once, yielding uniqueness and global optimality. Explicit evaluation at time one produces the sharp variance threshold. The Brownian order has negative endpoint derivative for every finite noise. A supplementary independently implemented quadrature and stationarity checker passed 3653 assertions. The continuum theorem does not rely on finite tests.

value.rationale: Optimal placement of one costly Gaussian trajectory observation for the entire integral is a natural, non-arbitrary probabilistic quadrature design. The global, exact threshold produces a qualitative roughness transition: all alpha>0 have a finite noise level at which the final time becomes optimal, whereas Brownian alpha=0 never does at finite variance. It also supplies a reliable one-root solver for the interior design across all real orders and factorial-dependent calibration for integer integrated-Wiener models. No general multiple-sample guarantee is claimed.
